sections.description:
Short title and commencement

CHIEF EXECUTIVE'S ORDER 6 OF 2000
BUDGETARY
PROVISIONS ORDER, 2000
CHIEF EXECUTIVE'S
ORDER 6 OF 2000
An Order to provide
for certain budgetary provisions
[Gazette of Pakistan,
Extraordinary, Part I, 9th May, 2000]
No.2-8/2000-Min-I, dated 9th May,
2000.--Whereas it is expedient to provide for certain budgetary provisions for
the purposes hereinafter appearing;
1. Short titles, and
commencement.--(1) This Order may be called the Budgetary Provisions Order,
2000.
(2) It shall come into force at
once and shall be deemed to have taken effect on the twelfth day of October,
1999.

sections.shortTitle: Chief Executive Order 6 Budgetary Provisions Order 2000
sections.description:
Preparation of Annual Budget Statement etc

CHIEF EXECUTIVE'S ORDER 6 OF 2000
BUDGETARY
PROVISIONS ORDER, 2000
CHIEF EXECUTIVE'S
ORDER 6 OF 2000
An Order to provide
for certain budgetary provisions
[Gazette of Pakistan,
Extraordinary, Part I, 9th May, 2000]
No.2-8/2000-Min-I, dated 9th May,
2000.--Whereas it is expedient to provide for certain budgetary provisions for
the purposes hereinafter appearing;
2. Preparation of Annual
Budget Statement etc:--(1) The Federal Government and a Provincial
Government shall, in respect of a financial year, cause to be prepared before
the commencement of that year an Annual Budget Statement specifying the
estimated receipts into, and the estimated expenditure from, the Federal
Consolidated Fund or, as the case may be, the Provincial Consolidated Fund in
the same manner as an Annual Budget Statement used to be prepared before the
issue of the Proclamation and may, in like manner, prepare Supplementary Budget
Statement and Excess Budget Statements.
(2) The Chief Executive and the
Governor of a Province shall also cause to be prepared a schedule of the
estimated expenditure from the Federal Consolidated Fund or, as the case may
be, the Provincial Consolidated Fund in the same form as that of the Annual
Budget Statement in so far as it relates to expenditure and shall, by his
signature, authenticate the schedule which shall be called the Schedule of
Authorised Expenditure.
(3) The Schedule of Authorised
Expenditure, as authenticated by the Chief Executive and the Governor of a
Province shall be the authority for withdrawal of moneys from the Federal
Consolidated Fund or, as the case may be, the Provincial Consolidated Fund of
the Province.
